- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a recent spike (e.g., >70) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing upward momentum — if true price rises >1.5% from prior day, adjust forecast up by 0.5–1.0% for next period.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-day moving average of forecast is >10% above true price, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with recent mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates final price — apply 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment remains positive or volatility is high.
